### Fixed
- **klaus-gateway reaches the kube-apiserver for its team-review endpoint on the bolt link store** (giantswarm/agent-platform#511; towards giantswarm/klaus-gateway#273): klaus-gateway >= 1.11.0 verifies every caller of `POST /reviews` and `POST /notices` with an `authentication.k8s.io/v1 TokenReview`, but the connectivity chart granted the gateway pod the `kube-apiserver` entity only for the Secret link store (`klausGateway.obo.store: secret` with OBO on), so an installation that keeps its links in the bolt store and turns `klausGateway.reviews.enabled` on had no rule to the API server in its Cilium default-deny egress — every TokenReview timed out and the endpoint answered 503 to every caller (the OBO policy's `world`/`cluster` :443 allowance never reaches the API server, which Cilium's socket-LB resolves to the control plane before the policy applies). `agent-platform.klausGateway.apiServerEgress` is truthy also while `klausGateway.reviews.enabled` is true, so `-klausgateway-store-egress` carries `toEntities: [kube-apiserver]` (cilium) or the `networkPolicy.kubernetes.apiServerCIDR` ipBlock (kubernetes) whatever the link store — one rule, rendered once next to the Secret store's. The connectivity chart declares `klausGateway.reviews` with the klaus-gateway chart's defaults (`enabled: false`, `audience: klaus-gateway`, `allowedCallers: []`); the default shape renders byte-identically. `make verify-klausgateway-netpol` holds the rule on the bolt store in both flavours, its absence with reviews off, and that reviews next to the Secret store render the rule once; `ci/test-klausgateway-reviews-values.yaml` lints the shape. Lab-verified in agentlab with the connectivity chart of the PR: the in-cluster gateway with `reviews.enabled` and an allow-list answered `POST /notices` from the allowed ServiceAccount with 201 and from a ServiceAccount outside the list with 403.
